title: On Helping the widow with her field
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：help　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 help 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the painter ① helped the widow with her field without complaint, and every visitor in the studio said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the painter ② helps the widow with her field with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ help the widow with her field at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ helped the widow with her field before — a line in the catalogue for May 1979 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Helping the widow with her field without complaint, the painter said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ help saying one cold word with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Help saying one cold word at once and never mention it again.

By 1992 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue, and a new visitor from the next studio ⑧ helps saying one cold word without complaint every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the easel, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ helped the widow with her field again when nobody else would.

⑩ To help the widow with her field, my mother said in 1997, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the studio remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the studio forgets, somebody helps the widow with her field with great care again and somebody must help the widow with her field without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 帮助（一般过去式 helped the widow with her field：1985 年画师头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 帮助（一般现在 helps the widow with her field：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 帮助（不定式 to help the widow with her field：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 帮助（过去完成时 had helped the widow with her field：1979 年五月的展品目录上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 帮助（动名词 helping the widow with her field 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 忍住（help saying one cold word：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去忍住忍住一句冷话不说）
G. v. 忍住（help saying one cold word：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 帮助（后段两处：新来的观者照例 helps saying one cold word，而母亲又一次 helped the widow with her field）

answers.why: help 意为“帮助”，1985 年画师毫无怨言地帮助帮那位寡妇料理田里的事，那是画室里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 helped。
help 意为“帮助”，自那以后画师小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 helps。
help 意为“帮助”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯帮助帮那位寡妇料理田里的事”，此处为不定式 to help the widow with her field。
help 意为“帮助”，展品目录里 五月 那行字说明早在 1992 年之前就有人帮助过，故用过去完成时 had helped。
help 意为“帮助”，画师说“帮助帮那位寡妇料理田里的事这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 helping the widow with her field 作主语。
help 意为“忍住”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去忍住忍住一句冷话不说”，should ever 之后用原形 help saying one cold word。
help 意为“忍住”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻忍住忍住一句冷话不说（help saying one cold word at once），以后再也不要提起。
help 意为“帮助”，新来的观者每个季度都照例忍住忍住一句冷话不说，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 helps。
help 意为“帮助”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地帮助帮那位寡妇料理田里的事，用一般过去式 helped 叙述。
help 意为“帮助”，结尾那句是母亲 1997 年的话：要帮助帮那位寡妇料理田里的事，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和画室记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 help 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1985 the painter helped the widow with her field without complaint, and nobody in the studio forgot it.
Even now the painter helps the widow with her field with great care whenever the studio asks.
Helping the widow with her field without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever help saying one cold word with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new visitor from the next studio helps saying one cold word without complaint every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother helped the widow with her field again, and the studio remembered that half.
